dervis-irab:22-26.t:
* I'rab:
(وَخَلَقَ اللَّهُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ) You may make the speech conjoined to what preceded, so that it serves as a proof of the denial of equality between the two groups, or you may make it resumptive (istiʾnāf), introduced for this purpose. (وخلق الله السموات): a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (والأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); and (بالحق) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent or of the object. (وَلِتُجْزى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām is causal; (تجزى) is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) أن after the causal lām. The speech is conjoined to His words (بالحق), because both the bāʾ and the lām can express cause, so the creation is given the recompense as its cause. Al-Zamakhsharī chose that it be conjoined to an omitted cause, its implied form being "so that He may show by it His power, and so that every soul may be recompensed". Ibn ʿAṭiyya chose that it be the lām of consequence or outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba / al-ṣayrūra), i.e. and the matter came to be such that by them some people were guided and by them others went astray — and this is not far-fetched. The wāw is of ḥāl; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (لا يظلمون) is its khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. (أَفَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلهَهُ هَواهُ وَأَضَلَّهُ اللَّهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ) The hamza is of interrogation intended as a command, i.e. "inform me". (رأيت) is a verb and its agent; (من) is the first object of (رأيت), and the second is omitted, its implied form being "guided" (مهتديا). The clause (اتخذ) is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; (إلهه) is the first object of (اتخذ) and (هواه) its second object. (أضله الله): a past verb, a fronted direct object and a postponed agent. (على علم) is a ḥāl of the object, and this is preferable to making it a ḥāl of the agent, as al-Jalāl parsed it; the meaning is: Allah led him astray while he knew the truth, because the intensification in this is greater and the censure and condemnation of him more. (وَخَتَمَ عَلى سَمْعِهِ وَقَلْبِهِ وَجَعَلَ عَلى بَصَرِهِ غِشاوَةً) Conjoined to what preceded; the discussion of this verse has already been given in al-Baqara. (فَمَنْ يَهْدِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ اللَّهِ أَفَلا تَذَكَّرُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (من) is an interrogative noun in the sense of negation, i.e. no one guides him, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ; the clause (يهديه) is the khabar; and (من بعد الله) are attached to (يهديه). The hamza is of disapproving interrogation (istifhām inkārī), and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted, implied clause, i.e. "do you persist in error?"; (لا) is negating, and (تذكرون) is an imperfect verb from which one of its two tāʾs has been dropped. (وَقالُوا: ما هِيَ إِلَّا حَياتُنَا الدُّنْيا نَمُوتُ وَنَحْيا وَما يُهْلِكُنا إِلَّا الدَّهْرُ) The wāw is resumptive, and the speech is resumptive, introduced to refute their claims, since they used to claim that the perishing of souls depends on the passing of days and nights — more of this discussion will come in the section on Benefits. (ما) is negating; (هي) is a mubtadaʾ; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (حياتنا) is a mubtadaʾ and (الدنيا) a khabar [Translator's note: so in the source; (الدنيا) is ordinarily parsed as an adjective of (حياتنا), which is the khabar of (هي)]. The clause (نموت) is resumptive, introduced to present more of their corrupt beliefs, and the clause (نحيا) is conjoined to it. The wāw is of ḥāl; (ما) is negating; (يهلكنا) is an imperfect verb and a fronted direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (الدهر) is the agent of (يهلكنا). (وَما لَهُمْ بِذلِكَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا يَظُنُّونَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (ما) is negating; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (بذلك) are attached to (علم); (من) is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (علم) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (إن) is negating, (هم) is a mubtadaʾ, (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and the clause (يظنون) is their khabar. (وَإِذا تُتْلى عَلَيْهِمْ آياتُنا بَيِّناتٍ ما كانَ حُجَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ قالُوا ائْتُوا بِآبائِنا إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; the clause (تتلى) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, and it is passive; (عليهم) are attached to (تتلى); (آياتنا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and (بيّنات) is a ḥāl, i.e. clear in their indication. (ما) is negating; (كان) is a defective past verb; (حجتهم) is the fronted khabar of (كان); (إلا) is a particle of restriction; and (أن قالوا): أن and what it governs are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of (كان); and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ائتوا) is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; (بآبائنا) are attached to (ائتوا); and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) is a defective past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the apodosis is omitted, its implied form being "then bring them"; (صادقين) is the khabar of (كنتم). (قُلِ اللَّهُ يُحْيِيكُمْ ثُمَّ يُمِيتُكُمْ ثُمَّ يَجْمَعُكُمْ إِلى يَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ) (قل) is an imperative verb; (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and the clause (يحييكم) its khabar; (ثم) is a conjunction of sequence with delay, pointing to the interval separating life and death; (يميتكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent (mustatir) agent and an object; (ثم) is a conjunction as before; (يجمعكم) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, and the kāf is the object; (إلى يوم القيامة) are attached to (يجمعكم). (لا) is the lā of generic negation, (ريب) is its noun and (فيه) its khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl of (يوم القيامة). (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) The wāw is of ḥāl; (لكن) and its noun, and the clause (لا يعلمون) is its khabar.

* Benefits:
Al-dahr (time) in the language is the duration of the world's existence, from "dahrahum amrun", i.e. time struck them with it. In al-Qāmūs: «dahrahum amrun, on the pattern of manaʿa: something hateful befell them; and they are madhūrun bihim and madhūrūn». It was the custom of the Arabs, when misfortune struck them, to ascribe it to time (al-dahr), believing that it is what does whatever it wills; and you see their poetry speaking out in complaint against time, so that this is found even in the poetry of Muslims. Ibn Durayd said in his Maqṣūra:
يا دهر إن لم تك عتبى فاتئد ... في إروادك والعتبى سوا
(O Time, if there is to be no making amends, then go gently in your pace — and making amends is the same.)
Abū al-ʿAlāʾ refuted the views of the Dahriyya (materialists) in his Luzūmiyyāt, saying:
ودان أناس بالجزاء وكونه ... وقال رجال إنما أنتم بقل
(Some people believed in recompense and its coming to pass, while other men said: you are nothing but herbage.)
This is a reply to the Dahriyya, who say that the world is eternal by nature, has always been so, and did not come into being through the act of an originator, and that people are like plants: they sprout and return through death to dry stubble. Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said, refuting Ibn al-Rāwandī and his book al-Tāj, in Risālat al-Ghufrān, among what he said: «As for Ibn al-Rāwandī, he was not guided to what is right; and as for his Crown (Tāj), it is not fit to be even a sandal. Is his Crown anything but as the soothsayer woman said: "Uff and tuff, a sock and a slipper"?» And the Prophet ﷺ said: «Do not revile time, for Allah is time», i.e. because He, the Exalted, is the One who does whatever He wills, not time. The ḥadīth was narrated by al-Bukhārī, Muslim and others from Abū Hurayra.

dervis-irab:27-31.t:
* Vocabulary:
(جاثِيَةً) One says: jathā ʿalā rukbatayhi juthuwwan (he knelt on his knees); I saw him kneeling (jāthiyan) before him, and I saw them kneeling (juthiyyan) at his side. In the ḥadīth: «I shall be the first to kneel for the dispute before Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection». They knelt facing one another on their knees (tajāthaw), and he knelt facing his opponent (ajāthā khaṣmahu mujāthātan); and so-and-so became a juthwa (heap) of earth. Ṭarafa said:
ترى جثوتين من تراب عليهما ... صفائح صمّ من صفيح منضّد
(You see two heaps of earth upon which lie hard slabs, from stacked slabs.)
That is: I see the grave of the miser and of the generous man as two mounds of earth with broad hard stones upon them, among graves upon which broad stones have been stacked. The wording of al-Qurṭubī: «There are five interpretations of al-jāthiya. The first: Mujāhid said: crouching ready (mustawfiza); Sufyān said: the one crouching ready is the one of whom nothing touches the ground but his knees and the tips of his fingers; al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: and that is at the Reckoning. The second: gathered together, said by Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is, you see the people of every religion gathered together. The third: set apart, said by ʿIkrima. The fourth: humbled, in the dialect of Quraysh. The fifth: kneeling on the knees, said by al-Ḥasan. Al-juthuww is sitting on the knees; one says jathā ʿalā rukbatayhi yajthū and yajthī, juthuwwan and juthiyyan, on the pattern fuʿūl in both; this has already been discussed in Maryam. The origin of al-juthwa is a group of anything. Then it was said that it is specific to the disbelievers, said by Yaḥyā ibn Sallām; and it was said that it is general for the believer and the disbeliever, awaiting the Reckoning. Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd Allāh that the Prophet ﷺ said: It is as though I see you kneeling on your knees short of Hell.» Further, it has been read jādhiya, with dhāl; and al-judhuww is more of a crouching-ready posture than al-juthuww, because the jādhī is the one who sits on the tips of his toes.
(نَسْتَنْسِخُ) That is, We have the angels write down your deeds. In al-Asās:
«I copied (nasakhtu) my book from so-and-so's book, intasakhtuhu and istansakhtuhu, with the same meaning; and istinsākh can mean having something written (istiktāb): "Indeed We were having written down (nastansikhu)". This is an old copy (nuskha) and old copies (nusakh).» The meaning is: We command the angels to copy what you used to do and to record it; so what is meant by naskh here is not cancelling one thing and putting another in its place.

* I'rab:
(وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) Resumptive speech, introduced to generalise the power after specifying it with giving life, causing death and gathering, because the meaning of owner is one who disposes of what he owns as he wills. (لله) is a fronted khabar (predicate), and (ملك السموات والأرض) is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَخْسَرُ الْمُبْطِلُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; (يوم) is an adverb attached to (يخسر); the clause (تقوم الساعة) is in the position of genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (يومئذ) is an adverb annexed to its like, and it is a badal (substitute) of (يوم تقوم); the tanwīn in (يومئذ) is a tanwīn of compensation for a clause, i.e. "the day the Hour is established". It was also said that what governs (ويوم تقوم) is what (الملك) indicates; they said: because the heaven and the earth will be changed, so it is as though it were said "and to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and the dominion on the Day of Resurrection"; on this view (يومئذ) is accusative by (يخسر). (يخسر المبطلون): a verb and its fāʿil (agent). (وَتَرى كُلَّ أُمَّةٍ جاثِيَةً، كُلُّ أُمَّةٍ تُدْعى إِلى كِتابِهَا) The wāw is a conjunction; (ترى) is an imperfect verb with a latent (mustatir) agent, its implied form being "you"; (كل أمة) is a first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) if the seeing is cognitive, but the context of the speech favours its being visual; (جاثية) is a second object on the first view and a ḥāl (circumstantial) on the second. (كل أمة) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (تدعى إلى كتابها) is the khabar. (الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (تجزون); (تجزون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (ما) is the second object of (تجزون); and the clause is the object of an omitted saying, i.e. it will be said to them: "Today you are recompensed". (كان) and its noun, and the clause (تعملون) is its khabar; and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (هذا كِتابُنا يَنْطِقُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِالْحَقِّ) (هذا) is a mubtadaʾ, (كتابنا) a khabar, and the clause (ينطق) a second khabar or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. It is also permissible for (كتابنا) to be a badal of (هذا), with the clause (ينطق) as the khabar of (هذا). (بالحق) is a ḥāl, and (عليكم) are attached to (ينطق). The meaning of the book's speaking will come in the section on Rhetoric. (إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنْسِخُ ما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) (إن) and its noun; the clause (كنّا) is the khabar of (إنّا); the clause (نستنسخ) is the khabar of (كنّا); (ما) is a direct object; the clause (كنتم) is the ṣila of (ما); and the clause (تعملون) is the khabar of (كنتم). (فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحاتِ فَيُدْخِلُهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (أما) is a particle of condition and of detailing the summary understood from His words (ينطق عليكم بالحق) or from (تجزون); (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila of the relative noun; (عملوا الصالحات) is conjoined to (آمنوا). (فيدخلهم): the fāʾ links the apodosis of (أما), and the clause (يدخلهم ربهم في رحمته) is the khabar of (الذين). (ذلِكَ هُوَ الْفَوْزُ الْمُبِينُ) Its i'rab has been given many times. (وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَفَلَمْ تَكُنْ آياتِي تُتْلى عَلَيْكُمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; (أما) is a particle of condition and detailing; (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (كفروا) is the ṣila; and the apodosis of (أما) is omitted, its implied form being "then it will be said to them". The hamza is of interrogation, and the fāʾ is conjoined to the omitted apodosis; (لم) is a particle of negation, conversion [to past meaning] and jussive; (تكن) is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by (لم); the meaning is "did not My messengers come to you, and were not…". (آياتي) is the noun of (تكن), and the clause (تتلى عليكم) is its khabar. (فَاسْتَكْبَرْتُمْ وَكُنْتُمْ قَوْماً مُجْرِمِينَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; (استكبرتم) is a verb and its agent; (كنتم): (كان) and its noun; (قوما) is its khabar, and (مجرمين) is a naʿt (adjective) of (قوما).

* Rhetoric:
1- The implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His words «هذا كتابنا ينطق عليكم بالحق» there is an implicit metaphor: the book is likened to a witness who delivers his testimony truthfully; the thing to which it is likened is omitted, and one of its concomitants — speaking the testimony — is borrowed for it.
2- In His words «فيدخلهم في رحمته» there is a synecdochic trope (majāz mursal) whose relation is that of the occupant (al-ḥāliyya), i.e. into His Garden; because a person does not dwell in mercy, since it is an abstract notion; he dwells only in its place. So using "mercy" for its place is a trope in which the occupant is mentioned and the place is meant, and its relation is that of the occupant.

dervis-irab:32-37.t:
* I'rab:
(وَإِذا قِيلَ إِنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَالسَّاعَةُ لا رَيْبَ فِيها قُلْتُمْ ما نَدْرِي مَا السَّاعَةُ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the speech is conjoined to what preceded because it is part of what is said to them. (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition; (قيل) is a passive past verb, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it"; (إن) with its noun and khabar (predicate), and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). (الساعة) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (لا ريب فيها) is its khabar. It was also said that (الساعة) is conjoined to the position of (إن) and its noun together, because إن and its noun have a position, namely nominative by being the subject. (والساعة) was also read in the accusative, conjoined to (الوعد). The clause [ما الساعة] is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the two objects of (ندري), because the verb is suspended (ʿulliqat) by the interrogative. The clause (قلتم) has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (ما) is negating; (ندري) is a nominative imperfect verb; (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and (الساعة) is its khabar. (إِنْ نَظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنًّا وَما نَحْنُ بِمُسْتَيْقِنِينَ) (إن) is negating; (نظن) is a nominative imperfect verb; (إلا) is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and (ظنا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). This construction is one of the difficulties around which the grammarians and exegetes have hummed at length; we shall give you more on it in the section on Benefits. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negating mā; (نحن) is its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; and (مستيقنين) is genitive by the bāʾ in form and accusative in position as the khabar of (ما). (وَبَدا لَهُمْ سَيِّئاتُ ما عَمِلُوا وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) The wāw is resumptive; (بدا) is a past verb; (لهم) are attached to (بدا); (سيئات) is the fāʿil (agent); (ما) is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause (عملوا) is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما). (حاق بهم) is conjoined to (بدا لهم); (ما) is the agent of (حاق); the clause (كانوا) is the ṣila; (به) are attached to (يستهزئون); and the clause (يستهزئون) is the khabar of (كانوا). (وَقِيلَ الْيَوْمَ نَنْساكُمْ كَما نَسِيتُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا) The wāw is a conjunction; (قيل) is a passive past verb; (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (ننساكم); (كما) is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); (نسيتم) is a verb and its agent; (لقاء يومكم) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The adverb has been used broadly, so that what occurs in it is annexed to it, in the manner of His words "the plotting of the night" (makr al-layl). (هذا) is a naʿt of (يومكم) or a badal (substitute) of it. (وَمَأْواكُمُ النَّارُ وَما لَكُمْ مِنْ ناصِرِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; (مأواكم) is a fronted khabar and (النار) a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the reverse is permissible. The wāw is a conjunction; (ما) is negating; (لكم) is a fronted khabar; (من) is a redundant preposition; and (ناصرين) is genitive in form and nominative in position as a postponed mubtadaʾ. (ذلِكُمْ بِأَنَّكُمُ اتَّخَذْتُمْ آياتِ اللَّهِ هُزُواً) (ذلكم) is a mubtadaʾ, the reference being to the great punishment prepared for them. (بأنكم): أن and what is in its domain are in the position of genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are the khabar of (ذلك). (أن) and its noun, and the clause (اتخذتم) is its khabar; (آيات الله) is the first object of (اتخذتم), and (هزوا) is the second object of (اتخذتم). (وَغَرَّتْكُمُ الْحَياةُ الدُّنْيا) The wāw is a conjunction; (غرّتكم) is a past verb and a fronted direct object; (الحياة) is a postponed agent, and (الدنيا) is a naʿt of (الحياة). (فَالْيَوْمَ لا يُخْرَجُونَ مِنْها وَلا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ) The fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ that discloses an implied condition); (اليوم) is an adverb attached to (يخرجون); (لا) is negating; (يخرجون) is a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the deputy agent; (منها) are attached to (يخرجون). (ولا) is conjoined to what preceded; (هم) is a mubtadaʾ, and the clause (يستعتبون) is the khabar. (فَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ رَبِّ السَّماواتِ وَرَبِّ الْأَرْضِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ) The fāʾ is resumptive; (لله) is a fronted khabar and (الحمد) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (رب السموات) is a badal or naʿt of (لله), and likewise what follows it. (وَلَهُ الْكِبْرِياءُ فِي السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ) The wāw is a conjunction; (له) is a fronted khabar and (الكبرياء) a postponed mubtadaʾ; (في السموات) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (الكبرياء), and it may be attached to the [notion of] being established to which the first adverbial phrase is attached; some chose that it be attached to (الكبرياء) itself, because it is a maṣdar. (هو) is a mubtadaʾ, and (العزيز الحكيم) are two khabars of it.

* Rhetoric:
1- The synecdochic trope (al-majāz al-mursal) or the implicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-makniyya): in His words «وقيل اليوم ننساكم» etc. there is a majāz mursal whose relation is causality, because forgetting is the cause of leaving; when a thing is forgotten it is left and entirely neglected. Some said: it is also permissible to regard the pronoun of address as containing a metaphor by allusion (istiʿāra bi-l-kināya), likening them to a forgotten thing in their being left in the punishment and no heed being paid to them, with the attribution of forgetting being the indicator (qarīna) of the metaphor.
2- The shift of person (al-iltifāt): this is in His words «فاليوم لا يخرجون منها»; He shifted from address to the third person when He reached this state to which they had come, for they deserve to be dropped from the rank of being addressed, out of contempt and disdain for them.

* Benefits:
We pointed to the difficulty arising in His words, Exalted is He, «إن نظن إلا ظنا», because the emphatic maṣdar may not occur as an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh); one does not say "I did not strike except a striking", since it has no benefit, being equivalent to saying "I did not strike except I struck". It is established among the grammarians that the governing word may be emptied for whatever follows it of all the governed elements except the absolute object; so one does not say "I did not think except a thinking", because the locus of negation and affirmation — namely thinking — is one and the same, whereas restriction is conceivable only when their loci differ. The following is what the grammarians said:
Al-Mubarrad said: its origin is "we are nothing but thinking a thinking" (in naḥnu illā naẓunnu ẓannan). He means that the locus of negation is omitted, namely the speaker's being engaged in some act or other; that is the locus of negation, and the locus of affirmation is his thinking a thinking. So the word (إلا), though placed later in the wording, is placed earlier in the implied structure. The import of the restriction is the affirmation of conjecture for themselves and the negation of everything other than it; among everything other than it is certainty, and it is what is intended to be negated; but He negated everything other than conjecture absolutely, for emphasis in negating certainty, and for that reason it was reinforced by His words (وما نحن بمستيقنين).
As for Abū Ḥayyān, he interpreted it as the omission of an adjective of the maṣdar, so that it becomes specifying rather than emphatic, its implied form being "except a weak conjecture"; or as (نظن) being made to carry the meaning of "we believe" (naʿtaqidu), so that (ظنا) is a direct object.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: what is the meaning of His words (إن نظن إلا ظنا)? I say: its origin is "we think a thinking", and its meaning is the affirmation of conjecture together with the negation of everything else; and the negation of everything other than conjecture was further emphasised by His words: (وما نحن بمستيقنين).»
Abū Ḥayyān rebutted al-Zamakhsharī as is his habit, saying: «This is the speech of one who has no awareness of the grammatical rule that emptying [for the exception] occurs with all the governed elements — agent, object and others — except the emphatic maṣdar, for it does not occur with it.»
As for Abū al-Baqāʾ, he said: «Its implied form is "we are nothing but thinking a thinking", so (إلا) has been postponed; were it not for this implied form, the meaning would be "we do not think except a thinking". It was also said that it is in its proper place, because (نظن) may have the meaning of knowledge and of doubt, so doubt was excepted, i.e. we have no belief except doubt.»
